data.description:
## Summary

`verify_completion` / `verify_completion_start` called without an explicit `ref` verifies
against the store repository's checked-out `HEAD`. That checkout is the shared main
checkout, which routinely holds uncommitted operator WIP and is therefore deliberately
never fast-forwarded by agents. It can sit days behind `origin/main`.

When it does, the completion precheck cannot find a commit carrying the ticket's
`rebar-ticket:` trailer, and the gate returns `verdict: "FAIL"` **with `findings: null`
and no `COMPLETION_VERDICT` event written at all**. The caller is given a bare FAIL that
is indistinguishable from a genuine "acceptance criteria not met" judgement, with nothing
to read and nothing recorded.

## Evidence

Observed 2026-09-19 on tickets `f3b2-6bb8-a643-4025` and `1d89-2206-bb64-4d98`, both of
whose fixes had already merged (`e8bdeb9a813` and `9f67fcfef7a`, both reachable from
`origin/main` = `d5c325a4170`).

- `gate_status` for both jobs: `status: "passed"`, `verdict: "FAIL"`, `findings: null`.
- `verify_completion_status` for both: `{"ok": false, "verdict": "unsigned", "reason":
  "ticket has no signature"}` — which reports the *absence* of a signature, not the reason
  verification failed.
- `ls` of both ticket directories in the store: **zero** `COMPLETION_VERDICT.json` events.
  A real criteria judgement writes one — `9753-647b` accumulated 4 across its runs, each
  carrying a `criteria` array with per-criterion `met` booleans and citations.
- Shared main checkout `HEAD` at the time: `e900fa14ad5` (2026-09-19 00:40 UTC), roughly a
  day stale. `git merge-base --is-ancestor e8bdeb9a813 HEAD` → false; same for
  `9f67fcfef7a`.

Control: `16c9-a42d` and `5a31-8c91` were verified in the same session **with** an explicit
`ref=c93f61d216f`. Both produced `PASS`, a signed attestation, and a durable
`COMPLETION_VERDICT`. The only difference between the passing and failing runs is the
presence of `ref`.

Re-running both failing tickets with `ref=d5c325a4170dfee29af010164a1cc2e3289cdc83`
is the confirming test.

## Why this matters

The documented agent workflow forbids fast-forwarding the shared main checkout, so a stale
store `HEAD` is the *expected* steady state, not an edge case. That makes the defaulted-ref
path a trap: it fails routinely, and it fails in the one shape that gives the operator
nothing to act on. The observed cost is a full re-run of a 9-11 minute gate per occurrence,
plus the investigation to discover that the verdict was never about the criteria.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Completion verification that cannot find a trailer-carrying commit reachable from the
      resolved ref reports a distinct outcome from a criteria-based `FAIL`.
- [ ] That outcome names the resolved ref it searched.
- [ ] That outcome names the ticket id whose trailer it searched for.
- [ ] That outcome states that no commit carrying the trailer was reachable.
- [ ] `gate_status` exposes a non-null reason for a completion run that ends without a
      criteria judgement.
- [ ] A completion run that ends without a criteria judgement is distinguishable by the
      caller from one where criteria were judged and not met.
- [ ] A regression test covers the stale-ref precheck path end to end.
- [ ] Documentation states which ref completion verification resolves when `ref` is omitted.
data.title: Completion verification without an explicit ref silently verifies a stale store HEAD and reports FAIL with no findings
